mergeRequest.title: test: mock the OS keyring in every test binary
mergeRequest.description:
## What does this MR do?

Keeps every test, including ones not yet written, away from the developer's real OS keyring and git repository, without per-package setup.

**Keyring.** Since credentials moved to the OS keyring by default, `syncKeyring` deletes the stored keyring entry whenever a credential is cleared outside CI. `Test_getFromKeyring` and `Test_fileConfig_Set_Empty_Removes` clear `gitlab.com`'s token before any mock is installed, so `go test ./internal/config/...` (or `make test`, or a pre-push that reaches the package) on a Mac deletes `glab:gitlab.com:token` from the login keychain. Tests that build a blank config for `gitlab.com` also read the real token through the keyring fallback.

`internal/config` now installs go-keyring's mock at `init` when `testing.Testing()` reports a test binary. The keyring backend is process-global, and every test binary that links go-keyring also links `internal/config`, so one guard covers all tests. Tests that set up their own mock (`MockInit`, `MockInitWithError`) are unaffected, and production binaries never take the branch.

**Git hooks.** When tests run from lefthook's `pre-push`, git exports `GIT_DIR`. In a worktree that is an absolute path to the pushing repository, and the `git init` in `local_config_test.go` re-initialised it as bare (`core.bare = true`), breaking the checkout. The `Makefile` now unexports `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, which covers every test that hooks run through `make`.

`Test_LocalConfigDir` and `Test_LocalConfigFile` also assumed the package sits two levels inside a regular checkout, so they failed in a worktree. They now create their own repository.

## How to verify

- `make test` on macOS leaves `glab api user` working afterwards.
- From a worktree, `GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) make test` passes and leaves `git config core.bare` as `false`. Before this change it failed two tests and set `core.bare = true`.
